question: composite ledger-only credit
scope: All30 unique retained Strudel composite note outputs. All complete responses and contracts were read. Exclude analysis and repeats. This is the finite format population, not an estimate across formats or future tasks.
method: Use pinned official Strudel1.2 transpiler, mini, and core. Decode unmodified complete note/slow/sound chains and evaluate the original JavaScript numeric slow expressions. Query one declared lane period. Use whole event spans. Within a lane, merge only control-query fragments of the same whole event and pitch. Preserve separate lane events and all meaningful musical overlaps. Convert cycles to four beats per prompt convention. Read every ledger GN line independently. Compare exact multisets of voice/start/duration/pitch. Manually compare both representations with task requirements. Existing score checks provide supplemental component totals.
limitations: No audio engine or sample-bank test. Nominal event whole spans are the shared musical durations. Fragments with the same whole event span and pitch are one event, not repeated notes.
Voice prefixes retain the local lane convention; they are not public note identity.
Query one declared line period. Strudel patterns repeat; later repetitions are outside the finite task. Item slow operators can cross that period.
The fixed four-beat cycle is the task convention. setcpm(60) specifies cycles per minute, not quarter-note BPM.
All reviewed outputs violate some task requirement except seven controls. Wider parsing does not repair pitches, rest weights, or timing normalization.
Component accuracy is partial credit. The counterfactual has the same frozen checks and their weighting. It is not a new public-format conformance or musical-success metric.
A component ratio is partial credit, not full response success. All ledger task checks and decoded notation checks retain the existing musical contract.
Composite and native aggregate comparisons exclude analysis; family component weights differ. They do not replace per-cell primary paired estimates.
